title: Fleetway - retainer top-up + sovereignty & edge onboarding
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in; customer requests capacity uplift, EU+APAC sovereign edge pilot, and contract extension. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, latency targets, security requirements (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps: pricing update, security packet, pilot scope + benchmark window, and draft amendment.
action_items: Priya Nair: confirm expected Q3 traffic profile and peak RPS for 48h benchmark; due 2027-05-02
Diego Alvarez: prepare pilot benchmark plan (latency targets, token mix, sequence lengths) and runbook; due 2027-04-30
Maya Chen: send updated pricing and amended SOW draft for +30% retainer top-up; due 2027-05-03
Neha Rao: share SOC2 Type II report, KMS integration notes, and VPC checklist link; due 2027-04-27
next_steps: Redwood to share security packet (SOC2, penetration summary) via secure link
Schedule a 48-hour pilot window in early May for EU private edge nodes
Redwood to send pricing and amendment draft
Follow-up call to review pilot results week of 2027-05-09
transcript:
Meeting: Fleetway Retail - Renewal & expansion check-in
Start: 2027-04-25 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Neha Rao (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (CTO), Samir Patel (Infra), Lena Kowalski (Head of ML), Omar Idris (Procurement)
Links referenced: security packet https://redwood.docs/sec/fleetway, pilot spreadsheet https://redwood.docs/pilots/fleetway-bench.xlsx

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. Quick check: is this still 42 minutes on the calendar? We're tight but should cover the key points.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Yeah that's right, Maya. We have about 40 minutes — going to set expectations from Fleetway side: Q3 ramp, want to lock in more committed capacity and get EU and APAC sovereign edge options scoped.
[00:30] Diego Alvarez: Hi team. I'm Diego, I'll take the technical side for Redwood. We can walk through tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated vs private. First high level: how much uplift are you forecasting?
[00:44] Samir Patel: We're looking at roughly a 30% increase in volume vs current baseline, spikes up to ~450RPS for short windows, average token length roughly 120 tokens per request. Current commit is 1.2M token-hours per month but that's been fuzzy — Priya will confirm.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Yep I'll confirm exact numbers after the call. High level we want faster tail latency in EU (target p95 < 180ms) and APAC similar if possible. Also strong requirement for data residency in EU and APAC, so private nodes or VPC must be considered.
[01:24] Diego Alvarez: Okay that helps. For p95 <180ms we'll want either dedicated footprint in-region or a private deployment in the customer's cloud. Hosted multi-region can sometimes meet that, but tails and cold KV-cache misses can push latency up.
[01:45] Lena Kowalski: Quick question — when you say "private deployment" do you mean Redwood-managed control plane with customer VPC peering or totally on-prem? We need to know the network model.
[01:57] Diego Alvarez: Good call, Lena. Our Private mode has two flavors: a Redwood control plane + customer-managed VPC peering (most common) which keeps data path in the VPC and lets us push safe runtime updates; or an on-prem bundle for air-gapped installs. For EU sovereignty we'd recommend the VPC peering model initially — faster onboarding.
[02:17] Priya Nair: We prefer VPC peering. On-prem would be a last resort — a lot more procurement friction.
[02:24] Omar Idris: Procurement note — any change to data flow means we need auditability: KMS key usage, HSM if possible, and clear egress controls. We also have a compliance review window mid-May.
[02:36] Neha Rao: We can provide the SOC2 Type II report and KMS integration guide — I'll share links. Also Redwood supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and can provide audit logs for all inference calls.
[02:50] Maya Chen: To connect this to renewal: Fleetway's existing contract is up for renewal in late June. Customer asked for an amendment to increase committed retainer by ~30% and add region activation credits for EU and APAC for the first 90 days. We did similar for other customers.
[03:09] Priya Nair: Correct. Budget needs a clear SOW detailing activation costs vs unit costs — Samir will validate.
[03:18] Samir Patel: Also need to understand fallback behavior. If dedicated nodes degrade, do we fail over to hosted instances? What are the latency and cost implications?
[03:30] Diego Alvarez: We have a smart routing policy: failover to compatible model variants in hosted capacity with throttled traffic. That keeps the service online but can change p95. We can set rules: prefer private nodes, then dedicated, then hosted with automatic cutover thresholds.
[03:49] Lena Kowalski: And what about model version pinning? During pilot we need predictable model versions so results are comparable.
[03:56] Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can pin model versions per-route and we can snapshot model binary for the pilot. We also store per-route KV cache warmups so the benchmark is repeatable.
[04:10] Priya Nair: Great. On the security side, our internal team will want to review SSO/SAML integration and RBAC for team members. Also data retention — can we set shorter retention for inference logs?
[04:23] Neha Rao: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC and per-token RBAC controls. Logs retention is configurable on a per-customer basis; shorter retention windows are no problem, and we can mask PII in logs at ingestion if needed.
[04:36] Omar Idris: Is there any certification for EU data residency? Some of our auditors asked about data-at-rest encryption and regional guarantees.
[04:44] Maya Chen: We don't provide an explicit legal guarantee of residency beyond the customer-managed private deployment in-region, but we do support regional hosting and restricted egress. We can include contractual language in the amendment that restricts data movement.
[04:58] Priya Nair: We'll want that in the SOW.
[05:02] [Crosstalk: brief murmurs]
[05:10] Maya Chen: Ok let me pivot to pricing quickly. If we do a +30% retainer and cover region activation credits, initial numbers look like — I'll ballpark — a one-time activation for EU and APAC per-region of about $X,XXX and a monthly retainer uplift that reduces per-token unit costs. I'll send concrete numbers after the call.
[05:29] Omar Idris: We need line itemized costs — activation, reserved capacity, overages, and a mechanism for burst.
[05:37] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll provide amortized activation costs and burst pricing.
[05:41] Diego Alvarez: For the pilot: recommend a 48-hour continuous benchmark with traffic replay from your production trace (anonymized) — we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. Also we'll include cold-start sim to surface KV cache behavior.
[05:58] Lena Kowalski: 48 hours is fine. We'll need to know exact traffic windows to avoid interfering with live traffic. We can prepare a replay segment.
[06:08] Samir Patel: For replay we prefer a dedicated test project or a canary route to avoid impacting customers.
[06:14] Diego Alvarez: We'll coordinate with you on routing to a private pilot cluster that matches production model weights.
[06:21] Priya Nair: Timeline-wise, we need pilot completed before our governance review mid-May. Is that realistic?
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: If we start next week, yes. Provisioning EU private nodes takes 3-5 business days once VPC peering is completed. APAC similar but depends on region quota.
[06:40] Neha Rao: I'll send the VPC checklist and quota requirements today so Samir can begin provisioning.
[06:47] Priya Nair: Perfect.
[06:50] [00:07:00ish - brief pause while people review docs]
[07:05] Samir Patel: Small technical question: what GPU types do you run in private? We need to know if model quantization impacts latency.
[07:13] Diego Alvarez: We typically use Ampere A10G in private nodes for cost balance, and can run A100 variants if you need lower latency. We also support int8 and q4_0 quantizations — some workloads see negligible quality loss, but we can benchmark.
[07:31] Lena Kowalski: We will definitely test quantized variants during pilot — please include that in the runbook.
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: Will do. We'll include metrics for generation quality (exact-match sample checks, ROUGE-type diffs for longer responses).
[07:46] Priya Nair: Another ask — is there an option for a canary model that is cheaper and used for overflow traffic? We want to keep critical paths on the top-tier models.
[07:57] Diego Alvarez: Yes, routing policies can route overflow to a cheaper model variant; you can set percent thresholds and cost ceilings. That's built into Optimize recommendations too.
[08:08] Maya Chen: On contractual discussion: do you want a 12-month extension with the uplift or a shorter 6-month pilot then commit?
[08:17] Priya Nair: Procurement prefers 12 months but we want a trial clause: if pilot fails to meet p95 target we'll have an exit or price adjustment clause.
[08:27] Omar Idris: Need performance SLAs tied to credits. Legal will want objective metrics.
[08:33] Maya Chen: That's reasonable. We can draft an SLA with credits tied to p95 thresholds and KV cache warm metrics.
[08:41] [08:41 - 09:30 - slightly longer technical exchange on warmup scripts]
[09:45] Diego Alvarez: Small note on KV cache: cold misses for certain long-tail prompts can spike tokens — we'll document warmup strategy. Also we'll include a recommended prefix caching approach.
[09:58] Samir Patel: That sounds good.
[10:03] Priya Nair: Ok, I think we have alignment on pilot and contractual ask. A couple of minor blockers: APAC quota and procurement window. We'll need Redwood to be flexible on start date.
[10:15] Maya Chen: We'll aim to be flexible. We'll also include a staging window so you can sanity-check before the full 48-hour run.
[10:24] Lena Kowalski: On observability — we want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards. Does Redwood's console support that out of the box?
[10:34] Diego Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route dashboards and token-level cost attribution. We'll give you a read-only dashboard for the pilot and an exportable CSV.
[10:43] Priya Nair: Good. Also need to verify retention and masking options for logs during public demos.
[10:52] Neha Rao: We'll include masking rules in the security pack.
[10:56] [11:00 - 20s: brief side conversation about calendar invites]
[11:18] Maya Chen: To wrap up, let's recap the next steps — Priya, Samir will confirm the traffic traces and provisioning ETA; Diego and team will create the pilot runbook and benchmark plan; Neha will share security docs and the VPC checklist; Maya will send pricing and a draft amendment.
[11:35] Priya Nair: Correct. We'll aim to have the replay trace and traffic profile to you by 2027-05-02.
[11:41] Samir Patel: I'll start the VPC setup today once I have the checklist.
[11:46] Diego Alvarez: We'll draft the runbook by 2027-04-30 and propose pilot windows.
[11:51] Neha Rao: I'll share SOC2 and KMS notes by tomorrow (2027-04-27).
[11:58] Maya Chen: Great. Any other blockers?
[12:02] Omar Idris: One commercial question — if the pilot shows >10% worse p95 than target, will Redwood entertain a pricing concession?
[12:12] Maya Chen: We'll include an objective remediation clause in the amendment: if pilot fails to meet the agreed p95 margin we'll offer a one-time credit and a follow-up remediation plan. Exact language to be drafted by legal.
[12:26] Priya Nair: That will help with procurement.
[12:29] Maya Chen: OK, unless there's anything else we'll close. Thanks all.
[12:33] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone.
[12:35] Lena Kowalski: Thanks.
[12:36] [End 15:42 PDT]
